title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-v12
body:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for unit economics + token math + initial tier ideas. Not a final PRD - just numbers and intuition to iterate with growth/product.

ASSUMPTIONS (baseline):
- Two model classes: small (7B-13B quantized) and large (70B).
- Runtime: optimized quantized inference with Redwood runtime (KV cache + batching).
- GPU cost (effective blended): Dedicated/reserved = $3.00 / GPU-hour; Hosted/on-demand = $6.00 / GPU-hour (this includes amortized infra, network egress, licensing, ops overhead).
- Throughput (steady-state generation):
  * small: 1,000 tokens/sec/GPU (conservative for optimized 13B on H100/T4-like inference with batching) => 3.6M tokens/hour/GPU
  * large: 200 tokens/sec/GPU => 720k tokens/hour/GPU
- System overhead & infra (load balancers, storage, control plane, monitoring, retries) add ~20% cost on top of raw GPU cost.
- Customer support, SRE, billing, fraud detection allocated on top (S&M/Ops) ~10% of revenue target (handled later in margin).

RAW INFRA COST / 1M TOKENS (back-of-envelope):
- small model (blended GPU cost = $6/hr hosted):
  cost per hour = $6.00 -> tokens/hr = 3.6M -> cost per 1M tokens = $6 / 3.6 = $1.67
  add infra overhead 20% => $2.00 / 1M tokens
- large model (hosted $6/hr):
  cost per hour = $6.00 -> tokens/hr = 0.72M -> cost per 1M tokens = $6 / 0.72 = $8.33
  add infra overhead 20% => $10.00 / 1M tokens

Dedicated / reserved effective cost (blended $3/hr):
- small model: $3 / 3.6M * 1M = $0.83 -> +20% infra = $1.00 / 1M tokens
- large model: $3 / 0.72M * 1M = $4.17 -> +20% infra = $5.00 / 1M tokens

Add target gross margin (hosted): 50%+ for sustainable hosted business (cover sales, marketing, R&D). So suggested hosted price per 1M tokens: 
- small: $2.00 cost -> list $4.00 / 1M tokens (50% gross margin)
- large: $10.00 cost -> list $20.00 / 1M tokens (50% gross margin)

But market comps and perceived value: could price small model at $3 / 1M and large at $12-15 / 1M to be competitive. Need to test.

EMBEDDINGS (quick):
- Embedding generation is much cheaper; per-vector cost depends on model size and batch throughput. Back-of-envelope: compute cost ~ $0.0005 per 1k vectors (dedicated) -> hosted list price $0.002 / 1k vectors.
- Alternatively charge per 1M tokens context used to create embeddings (confusing for customers) - prefer per-1k-embedding metric.

EXAMPLE CUSTOMER SCENARIOS (monthly):
1) Developer prototype: 100k generation tokens / month (small model) -> cost to Redwood (hosted): 100k/1M * $2 = $0.20 -> list $0.40 (if $4/1M). Not worth deep sales; keep free credits.
2) Mid-stage startup: 50M gen tokens/month (small) -> cost = 50 * $2 = $100 -> list = 50 * $4 = $200 -> revenue/seat modest; good for PLG growth.
3) High-volume product: 1B gen tokens/month -> cost = 1000 * $2 = $2000 -> list = $4000. For large model mix, costs multiply.

TIER IDEAS (hosted):
- Free: 0-100k gen tokens/month + limited embeddings (onboarding credits)
- Developer: pay-as-you-go; $x per 1M tokens with volume discounts at 100M, 500M thresholds
- Startup: monthly bundle (committed) 100M tokens @ discounted rate + email support
- Business: 500M-2B tokens/month, SLA + higher throughput, can enable dedicated routing
- Enterprise / Dedicated: reserved capacity with commit-based pricing (blended lower $/1M token), enterprise SLA, VPC/private option, per-month recurring fee + overage at discounted rate

Sample pricing matrix (hosted list):
- Small model: $4 / 1M tokens (base), volume discounts: 10% @ 100M, 25% @ 500M, 40% @ 1B+
- Large model: $20 / 1M tokens (base), similar discounts by commit
- Embeddings: $0.002 / 1k vectors base, discounts on volume

Reserved / Dedicated offers:
- Offer committed GPU pool pricing. Example: commit $X/month for N GPUs -> ~50% lower $/1M token compared to hosted because we assume reserved cloud discounts and higher utilization.
- Example commitment: $10k/month reserved -> covers Y tokens -> convert to $/1M with same throughput math above. (Need specific engineering table to map GPU count <-> tokens/hr for supported models).

KEY UNIT ECON QUESTIONS / SENSITIVITIES:
- Throughput numbers are very sensitive to real-world batching distribution and tail latency SLOs. If typical request shapes are many short requests (chat tokens <-> prompt+response), throughput drops and effective $/1M rises. Need traffic shape bucketization and synthetic benchmarks.
- CUDA kernel and quantization improvements can shift small model throughput 2x -> halves cost. Keep model-by-model perf matrix updated.
- Cache hit rate (prefix caching) materially reduces cost for assistant-like flows with repeated prompts. Build incentives (cache enabled routes) or different pricing for cached responses?
- Network egress and storage costs for embeddings + logs can be non-trivial for huge customers; consider separate egress buckets or include in enterprise negotiation.

OPEN QUESTIONS / ACTION ITEMS:
- Run microbenchmarks for 3 representative models (7B quantized, 13B quantized, 70B) with real traffic shapes (chat vs long-form generation) to get real tokens/sec per GPU under Redwood runtime.
- Build a small calculator (sheet) that maps: model, GPU type, tokens/sec, GPU cost/hr -> $/1M tokens; include cache factor and SLO headroom.
- Decide default list price cadence: do we present per-1M tokens only, or also tokens per request / per-conversation pricing for chat to reduce confusion?
- Evaluate competitor published prices and keep a price elasticity experiment for Developer tier.

Notes to self: keep draft short for sharing in pricing sync. Miguel to add real benchmark numbers next week, Emily to sketch cost model for dedicated/reserved product.

Rough mental margin check: if we list small model at $4/1M and real cost is $2/1M => 50% gross margin. After S&M and G&A, contribution margin can be low for small customers but scale improves. That's okay for PLG funnel.

END.
